title: Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions in the SU(2) gauge theory of the Shastry-Sutherland Dirac spin liquids
abstract: We classify the fermion bilinears of the SU(2) gauge theory of the Shastry-Sutherland Dirac spin liquids under the spin-orbit-locked space group and treat the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interactions of SrCu$_2$(BO$_3$)$_2$ at leading order in $1/N$ and at one loop. At linear order DM can neither gap the spinons nor destabilize the SO(5) point above a scale $T^*$. Symmetry forbids every local gauge-singlet fermion mass at any order. Among the singlet bilinears, the in-plane couplings induce only a conserved spin current of dimension exactly 2, which sets $T^*=4λ\simeq0.03$-$0.17$ K, and the out-of-plane coupling only a flavored spin-2 current, irrelevant at a unitary critical point. DM-induced Yukawa couplings start below $2\%$ of the one that bounds the pseudocritical window. In zero field, measured samples order above $1$ K, at or above $T^*$. Below $T^*$, in a two-dimensional sample at the critical pressure, the Dirac cones reconstruct into a chirally protected $d$-wave quadratic band touching whose only gauge-singlet gap channels are the two valence-bond components and the scalar chirality. A one-loop flow, with the gauge field screened by the band touching, ends at $T^{**}\sim(0.03$-$0.1)λ$ on a ray containing valence-bond order for the material's exchange and for most random couplings, and otherwise on a gapped chiral $\mathbb{Z}_2$ spin liquid. The DM bias between the two plaquette patterns is at most of order $10^{-4}$, with a direction not fixed at $O(1/N)$, whereas non-magnetic quenched disorder couples a relevant random field to the plaquette doublet and none to the chirality. A field along $[100]$ induces a $(π,π)$ Néel moment linear in the field; a field along $[001]$ does not. This selection rule also holds in the dimer phase and is testable by $^{11}$B NMR under pressure.
summary: This theoretical work investigates the impact of Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions on the SU(2) gauge theory describing Shastry-Sutherland Dirac spin liquids. Using advanced field theory techniques, the authors show that these interactions constrain the low-energy spectrum, predicting a transition into either a valence-bond ordered state or a gapped $\mathbb{Z}_2$ spin liquid below a characteristic temperature scale $T^*$. This provides a detailed theoretical roadmap for understanding quantum criticality in frustrated quantum magnets.
main_problem: The paper classifies fermion bilinears within the SU(2) gauge theory describing Shastry-Sutherland Dirac spin liquids, focusing on the role of Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interactions.
main_result: DM interactions forbid local gauge-singlet fermion masses, and the system's low-energy physics is characterized by a crossover scale $T^*$ followed by a flow ending on either a valence-bond ordered ray or a gapped chiral $\mathbb{Z}_2$ spin liquid.
method: The analysis employs theoretical techniques including classifying fermion bilinears under a specific space group, treating DM interactions at leading order in $1/N$, and performing one-loop renormalization group flow calculations.
model_or_system: The study models the magnetic properties of the Shastry-Sutherland lattice, exemplified by the material $\text{SrCu}_2(\text{BO}_3)_2$, using an SU(2) gauge theory framework.
key_observables: Conserved spin current of dimension 2, crossover scales $T^*$ and $T^{**}$, and the nature of the reconstructed Dirac cones (e.g., $d$-wave quadratic band touching).
important_parameters: The DM interaction strength, the lattice coupling constants ($J, J'$), and external magnetic fields applied along [100] or [001].
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on treating DM interactions perturbatively at leading order in $1/N$ and at one loop, and assumes the validity of the continuum gauge theory description.
figures_summary: The notes mention figures detailing symmetry-allowed DM textures on the SS lattice, which dictate the allowed coupling patterns.
paper_structure: The paper is structured by first setting up the model Hamiltonian including DM terms, then performing symmetry analysis to constrain allowed DM textures, followed by deriving the low-energy effective theory via gauge theory and RG flow analysis.
why_interesting: The detailed analysis of symmetry constraints and the resulting low-energy effective field theory provides deep insights into how subtle interactions like DM terms dictate the fate of quantum critical points in frustrated magnets.
